text:
Tampa Bay arrives with the better underlying game. At five on five, TBL has taken 59% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in its games, against 53% for VGK, and its 2.58 expected goals against per 60 minutes edges Vegas's 2.62. Vegas leads on special teams, generating 0.89 expected power-play goals per game to Tampa's 0.66 while allowing 0.30 on the penalty kill to Tampa's 0.53. The model sees a tight game, TBL at 3.08 expected goals and VGK at 2.90.

Both teams are 4-1-0 in their last five, but the chances tell different stories. Tampa has out-created its opponent in all five, averaging 58% of the expected goals, even though its record could be better. Vegas has taken 49% of the expected goals over that stretch. Its 17-6 scoring edge during a three-game win streak owes plenty to finishing and goaltending, and the model counts that. In net, the projected starters are Andrei Vasilevskiy for TBL, at -0.25 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops beyond what the shots would suggest) this season after +23.15 last year, and Carter Hart for VGK, at +1.98 this season after -4.44 last year.

Among players to watch, Brandon Hagel has the best chance to score for TBL at 43%, with Nikita Kucherov at 36% and an 82% chance of a point. For Vegas, Mark Stone is the likeliest scorer at 31%, while Mitch Marner carries a six-game point streak into the game. Brett Howden plays his 500th NHL game, a milestone the model doesn't price.
